'''Obata Shrine''' (小俣神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha (auxiliary shrine)|1=Setsumatsusha}} of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyōke Daijingū|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Gekū) within {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}. It is Ranked 16th among the 16 sessha of Gekū<ref>Compiled by Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pages 11–13</ref>, and it is the only Gekū sessha located outside the {{ill|Miyagawa|en|Miyagawa|qid=Q1665818|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie)|1=Miyagawa}} on its western bank<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): page 54</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): page 65</ref>.
== Overview ==
{{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}{{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise|1=Ise, Mie}} Omata-cho, Motomachi 1072 (formerly Mie Prefecture [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Watarai District]] {{ill|Omata, Mie|ja|小俣町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omata, Mie|1=Q11458873|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11458873}} Uramachi 7281)<ref name="sk3">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 373</ref>.<ref>Sengūkan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Shikinen Sengū Memorial Sengūkan | 125 Shrines 5]" (Accessed October 11, 2013).</ref> It is located on the left bank (west bank) of the {{ill|Jirutani River|ja|汁谷川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jirutani River|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} terrace<ref name="sk3"/>.
The {{ill|precincts|ja|境内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/precincts|1=keidai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11429002}} are surrounded by stone walls<ref name="sk4">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 374</ref>. The {{ill|shrine building|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shrine building|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|1=Shinto architecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080012}} is in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=tamagaki|1=Sacred fences}} fence<ref name="sk4"/>. Omata Shrine is part of the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|1=Jingū Shikinen Sengū|1=Jingū Shikinen Sengū|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|qq=}} and is rebuilt every 20 years<ref name="sk4"/>. There is no {{ill|offertory box|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/offertory box|qid=Q135491444|1=Saisenbako}}. The precinct area is 333 {{ill|Pyeong|en|Pyeong|qid=Q706688|lt=tsubo|1=Pyeong}} (approximately 1,100.8 m²)<ref name="sk4"/>.
The name "Omata" derives from the {{ill|place name|ja|地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/place name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Toponym|qid=Q7884789}} around the shrine. While it is read as "Omata" (おまた) in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, it is pronounced "Obata" (おばた) today<ref name="sk3"/>. The presence of an {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|lt=Kōtai Jingū|lt=Outer Shrine|ja|外宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Outer Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 豊受大神宮}} auxiliary shrine in this region is due to the development of the lower Miyagawa River area by the {{ill|Watarai clan|ja|度会氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai clan|qq=}}<ref name="ic"/>. Although this shrine uniquely sits on the left bank of the Miyagawa among Outer Shrine-associated shrines, many shrines under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (the Inner Shrine) are also on this side, making it not particularly rare within the larger Ise Jingū context<ref name="sk4"/>. Locally, it is affectionately called "Inabe no Yashiro" or "Iname-san" (稲女さん)<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. These nicknames likely derive from the {{ill|Kami|lt=Kami|lt=Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/deity|qq=}} it enshrines<ref name="sk3"/>. There is a {{ill|custom|ja|風習|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/custom|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Social convention|qid=Q251777}} of visiting Omata Shrine during the {{ill|Ujigami|en|Ujigami|qid=Q767655|lt=Ujigami|1=Ujigami}} festival in the area<ref>Sakurai (1991): p. 294</ref>.
The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ukanomitama|ja|宇賀御魂神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}} (Ukanomitama no Kami)<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. Ukanomitama is the child of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} and {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qid=Q682306|1=Izanami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q682306}} and is revered as the {{ill|Guardian deities|lt=Guardian deities|lt=Guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guardian deity|qq=}} of {{ill|Bumper crop|en|Bumper crop|qid=Q4997332|lt=bountiful harvests|1=Bumper crop}}<ref name="ic"/>.
== History ==
According to the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Jingū, Omata Shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|1=Enchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97379316}} 5 (927)<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22</ref>. It is also mentioned in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingū Ritual Records|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyuke Daijingū Ritual Records|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延暦儀式帳|1=Enryaku Gishikichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q109596938}}'', indicating its existence since before {{ill|Enryaku|en|Enryaku|qid=Q1373176|lt=Enryaku|1=Enryaku}} 23 (804)<ref name="ic2"/>. The document notes that shrine priests were assigned to Omata Shrine, and offerings of {{ill|heihaku|ja|幣帛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/heihaku|1=Hanpei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11481885}} were presented by the {{ill|Ise Province|en|Ise Province|qid=Q864166|lt=Ise Province|1=Ise Province}} {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|qid=Q1351234|lt=provincial governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} during the {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai|1=Kinensai}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}<ref name="sk3"/>.
While Omata Shrine had close ties to Ise Jingū in {{ill|Ancient history|en|Ancient history|qid=Q41493|lt=ancient times|1=Ancient history}}, records ceased in the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|qid=Q12554|lt=late medieval period|1=Middle Ages}}, and it came to be known as "Hachioji" (八王子), regarded as a {{ill|Ubusunagami|en|Ubusunagami|qid=Q1392097|lt=Ubusunagami|1=Ubusunagami}}<ref name="sk4"/>.
[[File:Yahashira shrine, Obata.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Yahashira Shrine|lt=Yahashira Shrine|1=Hachioji Shrine|ja|八柱神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yahashira Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}} (formerly Hachioji)]]
In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|en|Kanbun (era)|qid=Q1146228|lt=Kanbun|1=Kanbun (era)}} 3, {{ill|June 27|en|June 27|qid=Q2664|lt=June 27 (lunar calendar)|1=June 27}} (Gregorian calendar: July 31, 1663), it was revived at its current site<ref name="sk4"/>. Since the site was already known as Hachioji, the shrine was reestablished alongside the existing Hachioji precinct<ref name="sk4"/>. In {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), disputes arose between the Jingū authority and the village regarding the management of the shrine grounds, which were resolved by dividing the precincts equally<ref>Sakurai (1991): p. 278</ref>. Although Hachioji was merged with {{ill|Kansha Shrine|ja|官舎神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kansha Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 43 (1910), its former site—east of Omata Shrine—still retains the {{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=Main hall|1=Honden}} and {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=worship hall|1=Haiden (Shinto)}}, maintained by local residents<ref name="sk4"/>.
== Access ==
Located within the {{ill|Human settlement|en|Human settlement|qid=Q486972|lt=settlement|1=Human settlement}} of Omata-cho Motomachi, an area that retains traces of the old {{ill|Ise pilgrimage road|ja|伊勢参宮街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise pilgrimage road|1=Ise Sangū Kaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11378967}}, it stands alongside {{ill|Saikō-ji|ja|西光寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saikō-ji|1=Q11308285|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11308285}} and {{ill|Yahashira Shrine|lt=Yahashira Shrine|1=Hachioji Shrine|ja|八柱神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yahashira Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}<ref name="ic"/>.
; Public Transport
* About 1 km south-southwest from {{ill|Omata Station (Mie)|ja|小俣駅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omata Station (Mie)|1=小俣駅|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11458880}} on the {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line|1=Yamada Line (Kintetsu)}}<ref name="sk3"/>.
* About 700 m southeast from {{ill|Miyagawa Station|en|Miyagawa Station|qid=Q117381|lt=Miyagawa Station|1=Miyagawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line|1=Sangū Line}} (operated by [[:en:JR Central|JR Central]])<ref name="sk3"/>.
* Approximately 4 minutes on foot (about 370 m) from {{ill|Miyakobashi Bus Stop|ja|宮古橋バス停|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakobashi Bus Stop|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} served by {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu|1=Mie Kotsu}} buses.
; By Car
* About 13 minutes (approx. 6.4 km) via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 32|ja|三重県道32号伊勢磯部線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 32|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 32|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357920}} (Okimichi Road) and {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 37|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357923}} from {{ill|Ise West Interchange|ja|伊勢西インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise West Interchange|1=Ise-nishi itnerchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884865}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway|1=Ise Expressway}}. The {{ill|Mie Prefecture Southern Driving School|ja|三重県南部自動車学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture Southern Driving School|1=Q11357731|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357731}} is nearby, and {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 428|ja|三重県道428号伊勢小俣松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 428|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 428|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357937}} passes close by.
